evidence.excerpt:
Can a vision model learn what words mean from pixels alone? We show that the
two largest DINOv3 vision transformers organize words rendered in images by
word meaning, despite being pretrained using self-supervision on images only,
without paired captions, class labels, or other language supervision. We derive word
representations from embedding differences between word images and matched
controls, then test whether semantically related words are neighbors within each
model's embedding space, while controlling for spelling similarity. We find that
brand names in the same industry group together, as do nouns from the same
semantic domain. Country-capital pairs exhibit consistent vector offsets, similarly
to word embeddings trained on text. These word representations also align with
the representations of the visual object categories they name. DINOv3-H and

evidence.excerpt:
We measure fourteen models (Table 1): four DINOv3 models and Web-DINO-1B, trained without
labels or captions on images alone, DINOv3-7B by self-distillation and the smaller three by distillation
from it (Siméoni et al., 2026; Fan et al., 2025); three DINOv2 models, the predecessors to DINOv3
(Oquab et al., 2024); three MAE models, trained by masked reconstruction (He et al., 2022); CLIP-B
and SigLIP2-B, trained with language supervision on image-caption pairs (Radford et al., 2021;
Tschannen et al., 2025); and an untrained ViT-B as the baseline for visual form alone. The encoder f
maps an image x to its final-layer class token, or for SigLIP2-B to the mean of its patch tokens, with
no projection head and no per-image normalization.

evidence.excerpt:
than by a general ability to recognize similar spellings. Insertions and deletions
provide less visual overlap because they change the word width and, with centered text, shift the
remaining letters (Appendix C.1).
Sensitivity to word form also does not predict semantic retrieval. SigLIP2-B achieves 100% top-10
accuracy for plural or base partners but only 18% for capitals, compared with 60% capital retrieval
in DINOv3-H. Conversely, the Qwen3 text encoders achieve 69–74% synonym accuracy but only
21–26% one-edit accuracy. Thus, strong retrieval of spelling-related words is neither necessary
nor sufficient for strong semantic retrieval. We therefore interpret semantic structure relative to the
untrained ViT-B baseline, which captures similarity arising from visual form alone.

The scope and possible sources of semantic knowledge.DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B exhibit
lexical semantic structure connecting written words to one another and to depicted object categories.
Not all relations are equally strong: Category membership and country-capital associations are more
clearly expressed than synonymy. Similarity and association are distinct (Hill et al., 2015), so factual
relationships do not imply equally strong synonym knowledge. These findings do not establish
taxonomic hierarchies or sentence-level composition. Nor do consistent offsets improve analogy
retrieval over the country-only baseline, reinforcing the distinction between geometric regularity and
analogical reasoning (Linzen, 2016).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports independent measurements from held-out lexical benchmarks, ImageNet visual class directions, and frozen external text and speech encoders (Qwen3, w2v-BERT), which corroborate the semantic structure found in DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Semantic retrieval benchmarks (country-capital, synonym, noun and brand category purity), word-class alignment with ImageNet visual directions, and cross-encoder alignment with frozen text and speech embeddings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Self-supervised image-only pretraining (DINO self-distillation or masked autoencoding) and contrastive image-text or image-speech finetuning with symmetric InfoNCE loss.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully calibrated to word-level and category-level semantic structure rather than sentence comprehension or general reasoning. The manuscript appropriately notes that factual associations and category membership are substantially stronger than synonym retrieval and that broad compositional clue combinations are not supported.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations across 14 vision models demonstrate distinct emerging semantic clustering in DINOv3-H/7B across partner retrieval, brand/noun category purity, and ImageNet visual direction alignment. The reported effect sizes markedly exceed untrained baselines and smaller or earlier self-supervised models under non-parametric permutation testing.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on held-out lexical benchmarks, visual class images, and independently trained language and speech models (Qwen3, w2v-BERT).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Orthogonal semantic retrieval benchmarks (WordNet categories, country-capital pairs, synonyms) and cross-modal alignment with ImageNet class visual representations and external frozen text/speech embeddings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pretraining self-supervision on images without language supervision (DINO self-distillation / masked autoencoding) and contrastive image-text/speech finetuning with InfoNCE loss on text-screened pairs.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including lack of evidence for compositionality, the possibility of training data containing co-occurring rendered text (e.g. from web/Instagram data), and that the origin of semantic structure remains an open mechanistic question.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology derives centered word directions by subtracting phase-scrambled matched controls across varied typography settings and background images, providing a rigorous control against low-level visual artifacts. Thorough spelling controls, including one-edit neighbor tests and length-matched permutation nulls, cleanly separate orthographic similarity from semantic organization.
primary.quality_rationale: The empirical findings are supported by disciplined experimental controls (matched visual baselines, spelling-overlap controls, background variation, and text-screened ImageNet and finetuning subsets). The claims are circumspect and fully aligned with the evidence provided.
primary.scoped_contribution: Demonstration that large self-supervised vision models (specifically DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B) encode semantic relations among rendered written words and align with depictions of named visual categories without paired language supervision.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The empirical findings are supported by disciplined experimental controls (matched visual baselines, spelling-overlap controls, background variation, and text-screened ImageNet and finetuning subsets). The claims are circumspect and fully aligned with the evidence provided.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including lack of evidence for compositionality, the possibility of training data containing co-occurring rendered text (e.g. from web/Instagram data), and that the origin of semantic structure remains an open mechanistic question.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
